target_customer: Spanish speaking consumers and immigrants in the United States
problem: Banks in the United States serve customers poorly in Spanish, and Latino customers face declined transactions from name mismatches and support only in English.
business_model: Neobank: interchange, cash advance and credit products with Spanish only support

founders.name: Trevor McKendrick
previous_startups: Top ranked US Spanish language Bible app (over 1 million users, acquired by Salem Media)
founders.background_notes: Source: YC page. Now founder and CEO of Hickory per YC page.

founders.name: Joshua Howland
founders.background_notes: Source: YC page; now founder and CEO of Hickory.

exit.reason: A Wise blog post quotes the CEO saying changing immigration patterns reduced demand; the company help center lists checking accounts closing automatically on February 27, 2026.

technical_complexity.rationale: Built on a partner bank with cards, onboarding and bilingual support; regulatory and fraud operations were heavier than the software.

defensibility.rationale: Spanish only service and trust in the community helped, but other neobanks could add Spanish support.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent was shown copying the wedge; other Spanish first neobanks such as Comun launched in 2022.

market_need_then: Seis reported opening accounts for over 500,000 people and 100,000 five star App Store reviews per a Wise post, which shows demand, and the launch on March 25, 2022 stressed 100 percent Spanish support.

identity.voice_and_tone: Spanish only service, mission to end dial number 2 for espanol

branding.brand_signature: End dial #2 for espanol mission line
branding.community_and_virality: More than 100,000 five star App Store reviews reported by a Wise post, and coverage on CNN Business affiliates in July 2022.

brand_strength.rationale: Clear Spanish only promise, national coverage and large review count, though the name meaning is not documented.

outcome_analysis: Seis reached more than 500,000 customer accounts, raised a 15 million dollar Series A in September 2022 and about 18.7 million in total per one database, then shut down in early 2026 with accounts closing on February 27. The CEO cited changing immigration patterns reducing demand; one report adds that Zelle access ended. The factors listed follow those stated reasons plus an inferred funding squeeze.
notes: seis.com returned 503 and several news pages returned 403; not worked around. Series A and seed amounts rest on Seedtable and CB Insights listings (single database), CB Insights total 18.7M over 5 rounds so 3.7M across other rounds including a mid 2021 seed and a March 2022 convertible note is unrecorded in amount. The Zelle reason comes from one search snippet and is unverified. Shutdown headline from FinTech Futures dated January 30, 2026 seen only as a search snippet. Competition list left empty: the Comun coverage found is dated late 2023, too late for a Winter 2022 company.
